items.title: 4 mayoral candidates clash on tariffs, transit and Ridgeway Plaza at Mississauga Board of Trade debate
items.summary: 4 candidates invited to Mississauga Board of Trade debate. The Mississauga Board of Trade debate debate invited four mayoral candidates (left to right) Bonnie Crombie, Dipika Damerla, Carolyn Parrish and Alvin Tedjo. S. trade tariffs, transit and issues surrounding Ridgeway Plaza at the Mississauga Board of Trade mayoral debate, co-hosted by CBC News at the Sheridan College Hazel McCallion Campus. The four candidates invited to the Sept. 25 event, moderated by CBC’s Nav Nanwa, were incumbent Carolyn Parrish, former mayor Bonnie Crombie, Ward 7 Coun. Dipika Damerla and Ward 2 Coun. Alvin Tedjo. Here’s a breakdown of where each candidate stands on the three issues. When asked how each candidate will protect Mississauga businesses amid the trade war with the United States, here’s how they responded. Bonnie Crombie: Pointed to her record as former mayor, stating that she attracted over $9 billion in investment which created tens of thousands of jobs. Her proposal includes offering interest free deferrals on property taxes, lowering business taxes, guaranteeing payment to city suppliers within 15 days, promoting buying local and continuing to attract foreign and domestic investment. Dipika Damerla: She highlighted that Mississauga ranks 23rd out of 24 Ontario cities for ease of doing business, according to a report by the Canadian Federation of Independent Business. She pledged to move the city from 23rd to 1st in ease of doing business to help tariff-impacted companies, create new jobs, consider property tax deferrals and support buying local.

items.title: Mississauga mayoral hopefuls to face off in debate as election race enters critical stretch
items.summary: With less than a month until voters choose Mississauga’s next mayor, four of the city’s leading candidates will take centre stage Thursday night for a highly anticipated debate that could help shape the outcome of one of Ontario’s most closely watched municipal races. The Mississauga mayoral debate, moderated by CityNews Toronto’s Mark McAllister, comes as the campaign enters a critical phase ahead of election day on Oct. 26. The race has attracted attention largely because it pits incumbent Carolyn Parrish against former three-term mayor Bonnie Crombie, while councillors Dipika Damerla and Alvin Tedjo continue to position themselves as alternatives to what they describe as the city’s political establishment. Fourteen candidates are officially running for mayor, though recent polling has suggested the contest is largely focused on Parrish, Crombie and Tedjo, with Damerla remaining in the mix and a sizable number of undecided voters still up for grabs. One of the key themes expected to emerge Thursday is transportation. Crombie recently unveiled a transit-focused platform that includes a proposal to extend Toronto’s Line 2 Bloor-Danforth subway west into Mississauga through Sherway Gardens and ultimately toward the city centre, arguing residents spend too much time stuck in traffic. She has also called for stronger commitments from Metrolinx and the province to complete the Hazel McCallion LRT. Damerla has centred much of her campaign on fiscal accountability and government oversight. Earlier this week, she renewed calls for Mississauga to establish an independent auditor general, saying the city needs stronger mechanisms to scrutinize spending and investigate complaints. Tedjo has continued to focus heavily on affordability, recently unveiling a platform that includes a two-year freeze on Mississauga’s share of residential property taxes and a proposal to permanently freeze municipal property tax increases for qualifying seniors.

Make, repair and reuse items during Circular Economy Month
items.summary: This October, find ways to reduce waste, save money and make your belongings last longer. Donate, recycle, repair and reuse items instead of throwing them away. Nearly 500 million kilograms of clothing and other textiles are thrown away in Canada each year. Many electronics are also discarded, even though almost two-thirds of them still work. Instead of buying new items this Circular Economy Month, choose to repair, share, donate or recycle them to extend their usefulness. A circular economy is about getting the most use out of the things we own by using them for longer. These small actions can reduce waste, help the environment and save money. Learn how to give your items a second life this October by participating in Circular Economy Month events throughout Mississauga. The City is partnering with Toronto and Region Conservation Authority’s Partners in Project Green program to host a collection drive from October 12 to 25. Residents can drop off unwanted clothing, textiles and electronics at collection bins located at one of 13 City facilities. items.title: Malton Station Loses VIA Rail Service Starting Late October
items.summary: According to Insauga, VIA Rail is ending train service at its Malton station on Derry Road East in north Mississauga, effective Oct. 25. The Crown corporation says the move is meant to improve overall travel times as part of a schedule review it announced in mid-September. That same review initially proposed permanently cutting all service to Guildwood station in Scarborough, but VIA Rail reversed course last Friday after backlash from commuters, meaning trains will keep serving that Toronto depot beyond Oct. 25. VIA Rail is also adjusting other stops along its Quebec City to Windsor corridor as part of the twice yearly review. Saturday service on trains 68 and 69 will be replaced by new departures on trains 668 and 669. VIA Rail says the revised schedule is meant to better match service with passenger demand and make the network more reliable and predictable.

items.title: Ward 5 Councillor Pushes Council to Study Mississauga's Illegal Dumping Hot Spots
items.summary: According to mississauga.com, Ward 5 Councillor Natalie Hart is bringing a motion to city council on Sept. 29 aimed at tackling illegal dumping and littering across Mississauga. The motion asks staff to study how the city can keep public spaces cleaner, covering parks, neighbourhoods and commercial areas alike. If council approves it, staff would identify locations where dumping keeps recurring and evaluate ways to address them, from changes in operational practices to site design and where waste bins are placed. The motion also directs staff to look at public education efforts, including multilingual communications, to help reach the city's diverse communities with information on proper waste disposal and reporting tools. Staff would additionally consider expanding the city's Be a Good Neighbour and neighbourhood standards pilot program, which has been running in Ward 5 since August 2025, to other parts of the city. The pilot's record so far could help shape how far the broader anti-dumping push extends.

items.title: Mississauga Joins National Push to Mark Truth and Reconciliation Day on Sept. 30
items.summary: According to Modern Mississauga, Canadians are marking the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation on Sept. 30, a day that coincides with Orange Shirt Day and its Every Child Matters message. Established in 2021, the day recognizes residential school Survivors, their families and their communities, while working to keep the history of residential schools from being forgotten. Canadians are encouraged to wear orange in honour of Survivors and in memory of the children who never returned home. In Ottawa, the Peace Tower and the Senate Building will be illuminated in orange throughout the evening to mark the occasion. APTN and the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation are also hosting a National Commemorative Gathering called Remembering the Children, open to Canadians who want to take part. The observance has grown from a grassroots initiative into a nationally recognized day of remembrance, education and reflection observed by individuals, organizations and communities across the country, including in Mississauga.

items.title: Judith Anne Palmer
items.summary: Mississauga, ON - Judith Anne (Judi) Palmer on September 11, 2026, after prevailing over much. Born July 27, 1937 in Sarnia. Beloved daughter of the late Horace and Mary Palmer. Dearly loved by her late siblings, brother, David (London, ON) and sister, Joan (Tually, Australia), and their families. Judi was born and raised in Sarnia, and was very active in music and sports there before leaving for Mississauga in the 1960's. Judi had a most happy and rewarding career teaching and consulting with the Peel Board. After retirement, she continued to enjoy varied interests including travel, opera, the theatre and gardening.
